---
description: "Score the unscored semantic checks in the MCP evaluate checklist (eval/*_checklist.json) using this repo's semantic_eval_prompt.txt, then regenerate the HTML/JSON report"
agent: agent
---

Score the MCP tool-quality checklist generated by `a365 develop-mcp evaluate --eval-engine none` (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for how it's produced), using your own judgment as the LLM instead of an external coding agent CLI.

Steps:

1. Find the checklist file in `eval/` (e.g. `eval/localhost-3000_checklist.json`). If more than one exists, ask which one to score.
2. Read [eval/semantic_eval_prompt.txt](../../eval/semantic_eval_prompt.txt) — it defines the exact scoring instructions and criteria to apply to every semantic check.
3. In the checklist JSON, for every check object where `"type": "Semantic"` and `"score": null`:
   - Evaluate the check's `prompt` against that tool's `name`, `description`, and `input_schema` (and, for parameter-level checks, the specific parameter's schema/description) in the same tool entry.
   - Fill in `"score"` with `true` or `false`.
   - Fill in `"reason"` with a concise, one-sentence justification for that score.
4. Do not modify any `"type": "Deterministic"` checks (already scored) or any other fields (`id`, `prompt`, `severity`, `category`, `issue_ids`, `impact_areas`, `remediation`).
5. Save the checklist file in place with the same structure, only `score`/`reason` filled in for previously-null semantic checks.
6. After saving, tell the user to re-run `npm run eval:offline` (or the equivalent `a365 develop-mcp evaluate` command) to regenerate `eval/<server-name>_eval_report.html` and `.json` from the now fully-scored checklist.
